scientific_boundary: This pass ranks and falsifies signal cases from published/open metadata. It does not claim raw-sample verification. Frequency allocation membership raises an RFI prior but does not identify a source by itself.

findings.title: MLc4 / MLc5 common-interferer fingerprint
findings.independent_check: UCLA reanalysis reports MLc4 in an OFF scan and identifies it as RFI; MLc5 has weaker OFF evidence but closely matches MLc4 morphology, and the nearly exact 4 MHz spacing suggests a common interferer.
findings.lesson: Same-target + same-drift + nearly integer frequency spacing can be a machine-family fingerprint rather than independent celestial evidence.

findings.title: All eight Ma et al. top signals fall inside known human-active spectrum allocations
findings.lesson: Band occupancy is a prior only; OFF-source, repeatability and cross-target recurrence remain decisive.

findings.title: ON-strong/OFF-weak appearance is not sufficient
findings.observations: A large GBT archive search found examples such as HIP 99572 at 1498.44515 MHz that look isolated and are strong in ON / weak in OFF, yet similar signals recur within 10 kHz in several unrelated stars with similar drift; the study ultimately attributed all visually inspected candidates to RFI.
findings.lesson: TESLA SWEEP must add cross-target recurrence and morphology-family matching, not only cadence ON/OFF gating.

findings.title: Number-like VLF patterns have a modern terrestrial control
findings.observations: Stanford AWESOME educational data describe lightning atmospherics, lightning-generated whistlers, and a high-pitched VLF navigation-beacon pattern heard as 1,2,3...1,2,3... from Russian transmitters.
findings.historical_firewall: This is NOT proposed as the source of Tesla's 1899 observation; the modern transmitters did not exist then. It demonstrates only that simple counting-like morphology is not unique to extraterrestrial or intelligent non-human sources.
findings.lesson: The Tesla Number Gate must compare candidate timing against natural impulsive propagation and man-made beacon cadence controls.

findings.title: 3I/ATLAS is a current high-volume adversarial control
findings.observations: SETI Institute ATA observations covered 1-9 GHz for more than seven hours; about 74 million initial narrowband detections were reduced to about 200 candidates and all were traced to terrestrial or Earth-orbiting technology.
findings.lesson: Use the public 3I/ATLAS products to test whether TESLA SWEEP can preserve moving-target sensitivity while rejecting huge RFI populations.

next_raw_data_queue.goal: Replay candidate morphology and cadence directly from the published candidate arrays.
Build temporal-structure controls for Tesla Number Gate from open VLF data.
Adversarial moving-target replay against a very large known-RFI population.
Freeze a holdout before tuning Tesla Sweep scoring thresholds.

escalation_rule: Only signals surviving OFF-source, cross-target recurrence, known-band/RFI, repeatability and independent-instrument gates may advance to REPEATING_UNEXPLAINED or higher.
